Kiran: Neem sticks, two paint tubes, a clay lump, cotton wool, glitter glue, a sponge, string!
Indrajit: Are you talking to yourself?
Kiran: Craft class tomorrow. Seven things. Neem sticks, two paint tubes...
Indrajit: Race you to the gate!
Kiran: Not now, bhaiya! Neem sticks, two paint tubes, clay lump, cotton... cotton...
Indrajit: Look, a butterfly!
Kiran: Oh, Indrajit! Now where was I? Cotton wool, glitter glue... what else?
Indrajit: How should I know?
Kiran stood at the door, counting on her fingers. She had only five.

qa.q: How many items did Kiran have to bring?
qa.a: Kiran had to bring seven items.

qa.q: What did Kiran feel when she could name only five items?
qa.a: Kiran felt annoyed and worried, since Indrajit's interruptions made two items slip away. 😰

qa.q: What alternative approach could Kiran use, and why?
qa.a: Kiran could write the seven items down when she hears them, or picture each one in a place at home. A written or pictured list stays even if someone interrupts.

qa.q: How does Indrajit see Kiran's chanting?
qa.a: Indrajit sees a sister talking to herself and joins in with a race and a butterfly, so Indrajit sees a game and does not realise it matters to Kiran.

grounding: A girl repeats seven craft items aloud all the way home, but the chanting works only for a while and two items are lost when her brother interrupts.

subtype: Approach: repeating the list aloud again and again [Action]
passage: On Thursday Mrs. Rao said we needed seven things for Friday's craft class: glue, scissors, chart paper, crayons, cotton, ribbon and glitter. I didn't have a pencil, so I made them into a chant. Glue-scissors-chart-crayons-cotton-ribbon-glitter. I chanted it through the school gate and down the lane, over and over, like a song on a bus. It worked, until our front door. My little brother Mohit jumped out shouting, "Trisha didi, look, I lost a tooth!" I looked. I admired the tooth. When I opened my mouth to tell Amma the list, only five things came out. Ribbon and cotton had run away. On Friday I sat with a cotton-less, ribbon-less cloud picture.

qa.q: Which two items did Trisha forget?
qa.a: Trisha forgot the ribbon and the cotton.

qa.q: How did Trisha feel when only five things came out?
qa.a: Trisha probably felt annoyed and a bit embarrassed, since the chant had worked all the way home.

qa.q: What other approach could have kept all seven items safe, and why?
qa.a: Trisha could have borrowed a pencil and written the list, because writing does not vanish when someone interrupts.

qa.q: How might Mohit see the lost list?
qa.a: Mohit was just excited about his tooth and probably had no idea his news chased two items out of Trisha's head.

grounding: It shows a girl chanting seven craft items all the way home, which works until her brother interrupts and she forgets two.

passage:
Note to Irawati's class teacher
Ma'am, Irawati is bringing only five of the seven craft items today, and I want to explain. Yesterday she came home chanting the list, and I could hear her at the gate: glue, scissors, chart paper, sketch pens, thread, beads, cardboard. She went up the stairs still chanting. Then her brother called her to see a kite stuck on the water tank, and she ran up. When she came back she could remember everything except the thread and the beads. She was upset and kept saying she had it a minute ago. This morning we talked about writing lists down, and she has made a small notebook for next time. We will send the thread and beads on Monday.
- Disha, Irawati's mother

qa.q: What did Irawati's brother call her to see?
qa.a: Her brother called her to see a kite stuck on the water tank.

qa.q: How was Irawati feeling when she could not remember the thread and beads?
qa.a: She was upset and frustrated, repeating that she had the list a minute ago.

qa.q: What else could Irawati do the next time a list is given in class?
qa.a: She could write it in her new notebook in class before leaving, so the list does not depend on nothing interrupting her.

qa.q: How does the missing thread and beads look from the class teacher's side?
qa.a: The teacher may see a child without two items, but the note helps the teacher understand it was a memory slip, not carelessness.

grounding: It shows a girl repeating a list aloud, which holds for a while, and then losing two items after her brother interrupts.
